THE MoU TRAP · EPISODE 2/7
WHAT AN MoU REALLY BINDS
02
WHAT AN MoU BINDS,
AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
FACT
On its central commitment,
most MoUs bind no one.
RED TEAM
But in practice, an MoU creates four things
EXCLUSIVITYOver a site or a resource, sometimes for years.Competitors are kept out.
A TARIFF ANCHORAn indicative tariff or capacity, labelled non-binding.It becomes the reference point for every later negotiation.
PROMISES OF STATE HELPLand, permits, grid connection, support instruments.Expected before anyone has priced them.
A POLITICAL COMMITMENTA public signing, sometimes with a head of state.Harder to withdraw than any clause.
FACT
Three stages, three kinds of commitment
STAGE
WHAT BINDS
WHAT THE STATE HAS COMMITTED
MoU
Little in law; often exclusivity and confidentiality
A political signal; sometimes a site or a resource
Contract
Tariff, term and obligations of both parties, subject to conditions
Future payments, conditional on the plant reaching operation
Financial close
All of the above, now funded
Fixed obligations for the life of the contract
Source: author, Table 1.1
RED TEAM
The trap lies between
the MoU and financial close.
Some commitments never close. Others close on terms set when the project was least tested.
DECISION
Two tests are skipped at signature
THE LENDER'S TESTCan the project repay its debt?
THE STATE'S TESTCan the power system and the public finances carry the obligations for twenty years or more?
